#4853. Where Does Joe Burrow Live? Unpacking the Bengals Quarterback’s Real Estate Portfolio

He signed a record-breaking contract with the Cincinnati Bengals in 2023, but where does Joe Burrow live when he’s not on the field?

The NFL quarterback was born in Ames, Iowa, in 1996. His family moved to Ohio when he was eight, and he has resided mostly in the Buckeye State ever since. Burrow played for Ohio State University from 2015 to 2017, then transferred as a graduate student to Louisiana State University, where he won the Heisman Trophy shortly before graduating in December 2019. He was drafted into the NFL the following year by his hometown Bengals, with whom he inked a $36.1 million, four-year contract—plus a $23.9 million signing bonus. Three years later Burrow signed a $275 million five-year extension, making him the highest-paid player in NFL history at the time, according to ESPN.

It’s unsurprising, then, that Burrow has put down roots in the Buckeye State. Below, we’re examining the quarterback’s real estate portfolio.

In May 2020, a month after being selected first overall in the NFL Draft, Burrow revealed that he was spending the pandemic lockdown in his old bedroom at his parents’ house in The Plains, Ohio, just outside of Athens. Interior design apparently wasn’t at the forefront of his mind; the room still had his childhood Star Wars curtains and posters on the wall, though he had given the bed a king-size upgrade in high school, replacing the Star Wars comforter that once rounded out the room’s theme. According to The Sun, the 1997-built residence sits on a cul-de-sac and has four bedrooms and three bathrooms.

The Bengals play at Paycor Stadium, formerly known as Paul Brown Stadium.

In June 2020, Burrow spent $835,000 on his first house: a 2,900-square-foot Cincinnati dwelling just five miles from the Bengals’ home stadium. Located in the city’s historic Columbia-Tusculum area, the two-story property was built in 2014. Further details on the dwelling are scant—including whether or not Burrow still owns it. However, its location would make it a convenient place to stay during the NFL season.

#4852. BYD sold more EVs last month than the US did all quarter, topping 300,000

BYD sold over 300,000 electric vehicles in October, a new record and more than the US managed in the entire third quarter.

The world’s leading EV maker is showing no signs of slowing down. BYD sold 490,168 new energy vehicles (NEVs) in October, up 11% from the prior year and the company’s highest monthly total in 2026.

BYD’s battery electric vehicles drove the growth, with a record 305,743 units sold, up 37% year over year and marking the first time its EV sales have crossed the 300,000 mark.

To put that into perspective, just over 262,500 EVs were sold in the US in the entire third quarter combined, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates.

October marked BYD’s sixth straight month of higher sales growth and its third straight month of higher EV sales. Through October, BYD sold 1,953,700 electric vehicles, up 6% from the same period last year.

BYD’s all-electric vehicles (EVs) accounted for about 63% of total sales last month. Plug-in hybrid vehicles, meanwhile, fell 17% in October to 177,382 units. Through October, BYD’s PHEV sales fell 11% to 1,625,969 units.

According to BYD’s filing, the company exported 170,194 vehicles in October as it expands overseas to drive growth in markets like Europe, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America.

Through October, BYD exported over 1.5 million electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, nearly double compared to last year.

By the end of 2026, BYD expects overseas shipments to reach about 2 million vehicles. In 2027, that number is expected to rise to more than 2.5 million vehicles.

Market is in transition. BYD is dominant, but Geely and others have strong portfolios as well. Legacy manufacturers are slow walking, constrained by habit and unable to make critical strategic decisions in the face of the onslaught.

With several new and updated vehicles launching with its new Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging technology, BYD aims to continue attracting new buyers with longer range, faster charging, and more tech-oriented models.

While the US is coming off its best quarter of the year in EV sales, BYD’s performance shows how far ahead China is in the transition to electric vehicles.

China continues to lead the global EV market, accounting for over half of all electric cars sold worldwide.

With a wave of low-cost domestic brands flooding China’s market, BYD and other automakers are driving growth overseas in major markets like Europe, South Korea, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America, where legacy OEMs are already falling behind quickly.

#4851. The 11 Best Golf Bags Our Gear Editors Have Tested

It's time to retire your ancient, beat-up golf bag once and for all.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

WHILE YOU MAY not think about it, in many ways a golf bag can make or break your golf game. Sure it doesn't have any real performance value like a set of golf clubs or golf shoes do, but what makes a golf bag so important is its ability to help you carry your gear from point A to point B, with as little energy exerted as possible. And, if you’ve ever walked a full round of 18 with a crummy bag, then you’ll know exactly how it can take a toll on your game.

But, the best golf bag is going to be one you hardly notice. Confusing? Think about how a bad golf bag can impact your play. Maybe the shoulder strap always digs into your neck when carrying. Or perhaps your bag is too thin and flimsy, so you have to wrangle the heck out of it so it will stay put on the back of the cart. Poorly made kickstand or clubs don't go in and out smoothly? Not enough storage capacity to carry all your gear like rangefinders, your phone, and everything in between. That’s just the tip of the iceberg.

From an aesthetic perspective, you’ll want to opt for a golf bag that fits your stylistic choice, and on today’s market, there’s an option for every personality. Plus, thanks to the boom of golf in the last few years, finding a golf bag with style points is not a problem, especially as more and more brands emerge with an emphasis on visuals and aesthetics. We're seeing some truly standout designs from brands we absolutely love. Ahead, we've pulled together our latest guide to the best golf bags based on years of testing we've been doing on the course and at the range.

You really can't go wrong with a Callaway golf bag, but when it comes to which one provides the biggest bang for its buck, it's the flagship Fairway C. The newly designed model includes boosted storage all around, from the clubs (it can hold at least 14) to the pockets (7 spacious zippered compartments). What's amazing is the Fairway C still maintains a slim silhouette and a lightweight design (just four pounds in weight total). The bag is also waterproofed to the nines thanks to its water-resistant material and seam-sealed zippers.

A few more elite features we like include: Boosted protection for clubs thanks to soft rubber dividers and hard Shaft Shield rubber, a flexible base made to better sit on different surfaces and slopes, and a comfortable dual strap system for carrying.

If you are looking for a bag that pushes the envelope on style and innovation, then this is a solid choice.

The Ping Hoofer has been one of the best stand bags for years because it's simply solid at what it does. The comfortable double strap carrying system is intuitive and simple to use, the leg mechanisms are smooth and have never caused me issues, and there are plenty of pockets and storage for both walking and riding.

I've logged lots of miles walking with this bag over my shoulders, and one standout is the water bottle holder—it's positioned in a perfect location for me to reach slightly down with my left hand to grab and swig while I'm walking. The stow-away rain hood is also extremely handy and has saved some wet rounds over the years. While neither of these features are exclusive to the Hoofer, they're done in smart and high-quality ways that make this bag a standout.

While it's not the lightest stand bag in our guide at 5.5 pounds, it's still only 5.5 pounds and I've never felt it's too heavy. And the versatility it provides by being a great cart bag is too important to ignore. I have quite a few friends who still have their Ping Hoofers made in the early 2000s, and while they have some wear and tear on them, these bags are made for the long haul.

Read More: Garmin Approach S70 Golf Watch Review

Sunday Golf has quickly risen as one of the top bag makers in the game. At the center of its lineup is the Loma Bag, an ultra-lightweight bag (under 2 lbs) that's perfect for carrying the essentials on a par 3 or for taking to the driving range. The Loma Bag is great for the golfer who is looking for a side bag for those previously stated uses, but to really have enough space to play a round with, we love the Loma XL.

Like the Loma Bag, the Loma XL is built to stay lightweight. The XL is heavier than the Loma Bag (3.4 pounds to 2 pounds), but still lighter than pretty much all other golf bags in this guide. The XL comes with a double strap for comfortable walking on the course, a three-way top divider for keeping up to eight clubs organized, and an insulated frosty pocket for keeping your cold ones, well, cold.

It's minimalist, making it great for beginners and for those who don't want to deal with clutter or deal with carrying too much weight. The downsides are, of course, the ability to only carry up to eight clubs. If you pack the bag too full, you also risk putting too much weight on the pop-out stands.

The price point of under $200 really sells the Loma XL as a value-driven pick. It's not a Big Bertha bag, but it will carry what you need for the course—all while making sure you stay lean and mean. Start here if you want a trimmed-down golf bag, or if you are a beginner to the game and are still working from a small rotation of clubs.

The Titleist Players bags are a golfer favorite through each iteration. The Players 5 Stand is a sturdy stand bag with a low profile, promising plenty of storage without getting too ridiculous in size and organization. You get plenty of storage space (full-length drink pockets and apparel pockets), Velcro spots for easy glove storage, and an overall weight of 4.3 pounds. And just like the iconic hat, you get the classic cursive styling on the side of the bag.

The new feature on the Players 5 (that wasn't on the Players 4 bag) is a five-way top cuff. The extra compartment for club organization allows the ability to carry a few more clubs, so bring on the extra wedges and woods.

Really the only downside to consider is the cost. The Players 5 is about $40 more than the Callaway Fairway C—a similar golf bag in terms of configuration. If you're willing to pay up just a little more, then you can do no wrong going with this timeless pick.

Vessel Golf has long made some of the best golf bags out there. For years the brand would make bags for Tour pros that just didn't receive labels (so under the radar). In the past few years, though, the Southern California company branched out to the direct-to-consumer market and the response has been overwhelmingly good.

The Lux Stand is a new 2025 model that redefines what a stand bag can be: a rotator stand system that creates an extremely stable base, an internal base divider that reduces club jams even when the legs are out, a matching cart strap sleeve for when you ride, an umbrella holder, and so much more.

We've had a tester trying this one out this summer and it has wowed in every aspect. The details are also premium at a price that's about $100 more than some of the other stand bags in our guide. But everything feels extremely bespoke and premium.

TaylorMade makes several types of golf bags for those who want a deluxe carrier, but really the brand shines the most with its Golf Pro Cart Bag. Its sub-$230 price tag makes it super affordable for a quality cart bag that has everything one would want: comfortable shoulder straps, ample club storage, and generous pocket space.

Its nylon material and streamlined pocket space makes it easy to move and carry. The bag also has a 14-way top. The downside is this bag is not very waterproof. There are no innovative features or special details on this bag that make it standout. Instead, this is a classic cart bag that will get the job done and look good on the course—all for a generous price point.

Amazon has a lot of wallet-friendly golf bags, but if you are going to go the affordable route it's best to avoid the cheapest of the cheap. This bag from GoHimal is just a tad more expensive than the other Amazon brands, yet it still promises a sub-$150 price.

It's built with a 14-way top, so you can stuff an entire set of clubs inside (although remember it's one club per slot so it can be limiting/frustrating). You get a double strap for better carrying and decent pocket space (it even comes with a cooler pocket). Most reviews deem the kickstand to be sturdy, which is significant due to the amount of cheap golf bags out there that have weak and wobbly stand legs. What's nice is even the bottom of the bag is strong and capable of staying upright in a golf cart.

One negative to consider is the polyester material of the bag. It's durable and tear-resistant, but it isn't super rain resistant. So the bag is prone to getting soaked. Second is the logo; though the "Himal" reading on the side isn't ugly (a lot of the cheap Amazon golf bags have tacky logos and designs), it still is super large and visible.

If you are a golfer on a budget, then this bag warrants a look. If you are rocking expensive clubs, look for a golf bag that has more protective reinforcement features and better rain resistance. That's the verdict.

Ghost Golf first caught our attention via its cool magnetic golf towel. It turns out Ghost makes a mean golf bag, too.

The Anyday Katana is a one-of-a-kind storage monster with tons of pocket space and a 14-club carrying capacity. Subtle features like velvet-wrapped top dividers and cooler-lined water bottle sleeves (on both sides) make days on the course that much more fun. The bag is outfitted with carbon fiber legs so it can stand with authority, and it comes in a waterproof material that has a beautiful leather-like texture.

If you want luxury and premium storage, this is your bag right here.

Stitch Golf improved upon its original SL2 bag by giving it nearly 50 percent more storage while still staying under 5 pounds. The expanded storage means smoother pulls and inserts of clubs from the bag, which goes a long way when you find yourself repeating that motion a zillion times throughout a full round of golf.

We also like the designated pocket space. There's a larger compartment for apparel (like rain gear), a magnetized ball pocket that can store up to 12 golf balls, and a felt-lined pocket to store your phone and valuables.

The coolest detail about Stitch Golf's bags? It's super easy and low cost to add personalization features. For $10 more, you can add an initial patch that reads either horizontal or vertical.

Malbon has a fantastic take on its golf style, sitting at the intersection of country club and streetwear that’s neither vintage golf nor luxury resort (it also doesn’t hurt to have Jason Day representing the brand on Tour, either). Yet, it can portray all of those vibes somehow, very well might I point out, and its forest green cart bag does just that. This bag looks like it would be right at home at Augusta National Golf Club just as it would at your local course. This bag is more than just a looker, as its textured PU leather build looks lux, yet is weather-resistant enough to handle rainy conditions—and a hood cover, too. Though its listed as a cart bag, it has removable padded shoulder straps if you decide to walk a round and plenty of zippered pockets to hold all of your gear.

When traveling with golf clubs, you absolutely have to make sure your clubs are protected. I've been testing out Vessel's latest Travel Case 2.0 and it hasn't disappointed. While hard cases will almost certainly provide near-guaranteed protection, they're not totally necessary and are more expensive.

What's great about this soft case from Vessel is that it breaks down to a tiny square the size of its base for super easy storing. When you're limited on space in the garage or even just in the hotel room during your travels, not having to figure out where the heck to store a giant plastic case on wheels is a situation you'll be glad to avoid.

There is a fully padded top, reinforced runner guards on the back, rugged wheels that glide easily, and compression straps to really help keep everything in place. Keep in mind you will need to pick up a travel club protector separately, but once you do you can travel anywhere on any flight with peace of mind that your clubs are well-protected.

Golf bags essentially fall into two categories: cart bags and stand bags.

A cart bag is meant for cart use, which means they're designed for carrying on the back of a golf cart or on a hand (or roller) cart when walking the course. Cart bags are usually larger and contain more organizational space. The downside is they're heavier and, hence the name, you need to rent a cart (or prepare for some serious energy exertion when carrying around a course, which we don't recommend).

A stand bag is meant for carrying on your back. They typically have better strap designs (double straps) and are more lightweight. They also have a kickstand for keeping the bag upright when setting the bag down to pull out your clubs. The downside to a stand bag is less club space (the bag has to accommodate a kickstand placement) and less pocket space. It should also be noted that stand bags can be used when riding in a cart or using a hand cart. These are the most common bags amateur golfers use and are our recommended choice for the versatility they offer.

The number of dividers on your golf bag depends on how many clubs you like to play with. If you play with a full set of 14 clubs (which is what most golfers typically do), a 14-way divider is not necessarily the way to go—this requires a more precise in-and-out grabbing of clubs as each divider can only house one club. This means you can't just toss a club in the bag and keep moving, which can slow things down and even frustrate at times.

The most common divider types are four- and five-way. A common theory to organizing your clubs easily utilizes this layout: woods in the big compartment, long and mid irons together, short irons and wedges together, and the flat stick (aka putter) in a slot on its own. While this is by no means a rule, grouping like clubs together is a simple way to make use of your bag's space.

It's worth mentioning waterproofing because this characteristic can raise or lower the overall price of a golf bag. If you're golfing a lot or have an expensive set of clubs, then it's probably worth investing in a waterproof bag (and certainly one with a rain hood). Some waterproof bags are better than others, with seam-taped zippers and waterproof pockets. Other bags usually just have water-resistant shells.

If you aren't golfing a lot or if you have a more inexpensive club set, then waterproof features might not be that important. You can save some money by opting for a golf bag that's not fully waterproof, then if you're caught in the rain while playing you can simply put a plastic poncho over your clubs or buy some sort of rain hood to help protect the clubs.

While I may not be the most avid golfer on our MH staff, the one thing I do ensure I am consistent with is staying up on golf trends and style, which also means knowing the latest gear and brands. This serves as an excellent baseline for my research to ensure each pick not only looks fantastic on the course, but will perform to the standards you need them to.

I also partnered with our Senior Gear and Reviews Editor Ryan Brower, who is an avid golfer, and a not-too-shabby mid-handicapper. Along with a few other golfers at Men's Health, we tested golf bags while walking 18, on 72-hole golf trips across the country, riding in carts, and playing pitch and putts.

We started with the golf bags we've been using and testing throughout the years, and then researched and got our hands on some new models as well as ones that we have yet to try out. We evaluated well over a dozen golf bags for this year's iteration of this guide based on comfort, durability, performance, and price point. Then we narrowed it down to the 11 best golf bags to satisfy any golfer's demands.

#4849. PMOS, Formerly PCOS, May Be Associated with Alzheimer's Disease Risk

Follow Healthline on our socials for all things health.

Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), has been linked to changes in brain function and cognition that may overlap with those seen in Alzheimer’s disease.

However, a review published October 13 in the Journal of the Endocrine Society suggests that metabolic conditions commonly associated with PMOS, rather than PMOS itself, may help explain a potential link to Alzheimer’s disease and dementia risk.

“Researchers are exploring whether some metabolic conditions commonly seen in women with PMOS, such as insulin resistance, obesity, type 2 diabetes, [and] elevated cholesterol, could play a role in dementia, since these are already known risk factors for cognitive decline,” Yesika Garcia, MD, board certified endocrinologist with Medical Offices of Manhattan, who was not involved in the study, told Healthline.

“In other words, any potential connection may be related to these underlying metabolic issues rather than PMOS itself. I think it’s important to clarify that an association does not mean causation,” she added.

The researchers searched PubMed for studies published through 2025 examining brain structure and function, cognitive performance, biomarkers associated with neurodegenerative diseases, and dementia risk in people with PMOS.

Because PMOS is a newer term, the researchers searched for studies using both PMOS and PCOS.

The review identified studies suggesting that people with PMOS may experience mild differences in certain cognitive abilities, including:

Some brain imaging studies using MRI and PET scans identified differences in brain structure and function among people with PMOS. Researchers also observed hormonal changes associated with differences in gray matter.

Some studies identified elevated biomarkers associated with Alzheimer’s disease in people with PMOS. These findings appeared to overlap with metabolic changes seen in type 2 diabetes, particularly those associated with obesity and insulin resistance.

The researchers also found that neurological differences were less pronounced when people with PMOS were compared with metabolically healthy control groups, suggesting that associated metabolic conditions may play an important role in these findings.

Overall, the review suggests that metabolic conditions associated with PMOS may contribute to changes in brain health, although more research is needed to determine whether PMOS independently affects Alzheimer’s disease or dementia risk.

“I think we need to be careful about drawing conclusions too early. The research raises some good questions, but it doesn’t prove that PCOS [PMOS] causes Alzheimer’s disease,” said Dung Trinh, MD, internist, of MemorialCare Medical Group and Chief Medical Officer of Healthy Brain Clinic in Irvine, CA, who wasn’t involved in the study.

“What it does reinforce is how important metabolic health may be when it comes to protecting our brains as we get older,” he added.

Sherry Ross, MD, board certified OB/GYN and Women’s Health Expert at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, who also wasn’t involved in the study, agreed. She also added that more attention and research need to be given to PMOS, brain changes, and future risks of dementia.

There are various ways that PMOS and dementia may share pathways and overlap, according to the researchers. Some of these shared pathways include:

Trinh explained that insulin resistance may be one of the most important connections between PMOS and dementia.

Although insulin is commonly associated with diabetes and blood sugar regulation, it also plays an important role in brain function. When insulin signaling doesn’t work properly, it may interfere with how brain cells use energy, potentially contributing to problems with memory and thinking over time.

Chronic inflammation, which can occur in people with PMOS, may also play a role in Alzheimer’s disease, Trinh told Healthline.

“Researchers are looking at how these metabolic changes may affect amyloid and tau, two proteins associated with Alzheimer’s. Some brain imaging studies have even found differences in brain structure and function among women with PCOS [PMOS],” he said.

Ross added that elevated androgen levels, which are common in people with PMOS, may also play a role in dementia risk.

“An important distinction is that these risk factors are not present in every woman with PMOS, and having PMOS does not automatically mean someone will experience cognitive decline,” cautioned Garcia.

Garcia noted that many of the dementia risk factors associated with PMOS are modifiable.

“Regular exercise, including both cardiovascular activity and strength training, can improve insulin sensitivity, help with weight management, and support cardiovascular and brain health,” she added.

“A Mediterranean-style diet, with plenty of vegetables, fruits, whole grains, healthy fats, and lean sources of protein, is a reasonable place to start,” he said.

Managing blood sugar, cholesterol, and blood pressure is also important, Trinh and Garcia noted.

“Medication, like metformin, can also improve insulin resistance, which may further reduce the risk of dementia,” Ross added.

Getting adequate sleep, avoiding smoking, and staying mentally and socially active are additional ways to support long-term brain health, Garcia told Healthline.

“For someone with PCOS [PMOS], I would encourage regular visits with their healthcare provider to monitor metabolic health and address problems early,” said Trinh.

“While we cannot say that these interventions specifically prevent dementia in women with PMOS, we know they benefit overall metabolic and cardiovascular health, which are closely connected to brain health,” explained Garcia.

Launching today, the two brands have joined forces on a 28-piece holiday capsule of heirloom-worthy wardrobe and home essentials inspired by The Six Bells’ vintage aesthetic. Pieces specifically pay homage to the hotel’s interiors through references to archival patterns and wallpaper prints found throughout the Inn’s rooms and communal spaces.

“We fell in love with [The Six Bells’] distinct, whimsical world—the mix of patterns, the nostalgic sentiment, and the personality in every detail,” says Madewell creative director Steven Cateron. During initial planning for the clothing brand’s holiday collection, the Rosendale, New York-based hotel became an unexpected source of inspiration for Cateron and his team because of the shared appreciation for heritage and storytelling. “Each piece has intention, whether it’s to wear day-to-day or for a celebration, a gifting moment for a loved one or hostess, or pajama pieces that lean into cozy season,” he says.

Sock slippers from the collaboration and Madewell’s classic denim make a perfect pairing.

Founded by Audrey Gelman in 2025, who designed the hotel in collaboration with interiors firm GrecoDeco, the Countryside Inn has quickly risen in popularity—even earning a spot in AD’s list of Great Design Hotels last year. “This project is so rooted in a shared love of the decorative arts and global human history,” designer Adam Greco previously told AD. Design-wise, maximalism dominates the interiors. Picture: rooms wrapped in fretwork wallpaper and deep cinnabar paint, with pistachio window shades and striped seating.

The collection also builds on the fantasy of Barrow’s Green, the fictional English village dreamed up by Gelman that includes its own imaginary landmarks and distinct locals (including a town gossip and poignant editor). “It was so interesting to broaden our fimaginations and think about how The Six Bells’ style could be brought to life through clothes,” says Gelman.

A cheeky message makes this classic needlepoint pillow pop.

At the same time, the collaboration was an opportunity to venture into Madwell’s less-explored categories—specifically the home space. The collection’s interior goods are a practice in curated nostalgia: There are holiday ornaments you’ll reach for year after year, scented candles and soaps to integrate into your daily winter routine, and cozy pajamas inspired by vintage sleep silhouettes. “If it’s something we don’t currently offer, we want to work with people that do the category best,” says Cateron. “The Six Bells team were the perfect partners to bring this collection’s home accessories to life.”

Still, versatility isn’t lost in the assortment. In designing the clothing, Cateron made sure to include “pieces to wear upstate, in the city, or for day-to-day celebrations.” Classic denim jackets are neutral staples that you can reach for any day of the week, while fair-isle wool knits are seasonally appropriate while still feeling adaptable enough to wear after the holidays. “There’s a real point of view behind every detail [at the Countryside Inn], from the interiors to collected vintage pieces,” says Cateron. “This collection captures that sensibility in a way that felt authentic to both brands.”

The collection is available to shop on Madewell.com and in Madewell stores starting today, November 12.

“There’s so much character in every detail at The Six Bells, and we wanted to bring that sensibility into each piece,” says Madewell creative director Steven Cateron.

#4847. Toyota’s Corolla Cross EV spotted for the first time [Images]

Toyota is giving its best-selling Corolla a major makeover, and an all-electric version is part of the plan. The upcoming Corolla Cross EV was captured in public for the first time ahead of its expected 2027 debut.

The Corolla has always been “a car for everyone,” Toyota’s former president and current CEO, Koji Sato, said after unveiling the next-gen Corolla Concept at last year’s Japan Mobility Show.

Since it went on sale 60 years ago, over 57 million drivers have chosen the Corolla, making it Toyota’s best-selling vehicle ever.

The Corolla has undergone 12 model changes since 1966, but the compact car is about to undergo its biggest transformation yet.

Although it’s still a top seller, the Corolla has lost some of its appeal as new, more advanced, and efficient options have emerged. Toyota looks to change that with the next-generation model.

It will remain “a car for everyone,” as Sato said, but the next-gen Corolla will come in multiple powertrains, including an all-electric version.

“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle―whatever the power source―let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive,” Sato said at the Japan Mobility Show last October.

Ahead of its expected debut sometime in 2027, a disguised Corolla Cross EV was spotted driving near Toyota’s European headquarters and R&D center.

New images from Chinese media outlet Autohome show what’s expected to be the all-electric Corolla Cross, with a closed-off grille and a unique body design.

The new Corolla will be the first to use Toyota’s new “multipathway” platform that will support electric, hybrid, gas, and other powertrains.

Toyota hasn’t revealed specifics, including battery or powertrain specs, but the next-gen Corolla EV is expected to remain close in style to the Concept. Aside from the massive COROLLA badge on the back, it looks like an entirely different vehicle with a near sports-car-like silhouette.

In an exclusive interview with Japanese media NHK in July, Toyota’s current chairman and former CEO, Akio Toyoda, warned that the company “cannot survive” if it does not adapt amid new competition and technology from China.

During the special, which went behind the scenes at Toyota’s “top secret” development site, several blurred Corolla Concept body types, including a sedan, hatchback, crossover, and GR model, were revealed in the background.

According to a recent Nikkei report, Toyota plans to begin production of the next-gen Corolla in 2028 through its joint venture with Chinese state-owned FAW Group, FAW Toyota Motor.

The Toyota Corolla EV is expected to be available in single- and dual-motor configurations with a driving range of at least 250 miles.

Let's hope that Toyota gets the Corolla EV right, because if it offers the right range for the right price but still feels fundamentally like a Corolla it is an EV that would get consideration from buyers who wouldn't otherwise consider an EV.

They're the buyers that trust Toyota and who consider the Corolla to be a nice safe choice for a car. And by safe, that means a vehicle that may not be all that exciting, but also a vehicle that they won't regret buying. Needless to say, these are not people who read Electrek, or even Car & Driver, for that matter. But there's a lot more of them than there are of us.

The hybrid version will reportedly use a new 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an electric motor. Toyota’s engineers told Car and Driver the system would deliver around 134 horsepower. It’s also estimated to be 10% to 20% more efficient than the current Corolla.

Toyota has yet to confirm the electric version will launch in the US. According to Car and Driver, the gas version will likely start at around $25,000, the hybrid around $27,000, and the EV and PHEVs will likely be priced in the $30,000 range.

#4846. Fall Weddings Are More Popular Than Ever. Here's How to Dress for One (The Right Way)

Autumn is now the most popular season to tie the knot.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

WEDDINGS CAN be hard to dress for, and this isn’t limited to those directly involved; being a mere attendant requires some degree of planning. I’ve attended quite a few weddings over the last year, both as a groomsman and as a regular guest, both with their own sartorial challenges. (I actually found it more stressful not being in the wedding party, at least in one aspect: I had to pick out my own outfit. This also allowed for a little creativity.)

I covered some options for summer weddings a few months back, and just like that, we’re on to the next season. Fall has arguably become the season for weddings; in fact, October recently overtook June as the most popular month for weddings in the U.S. I can attest to this; I was in two separate ones last October.

Summer and fall weddings have quite a few differences. You can get away with some more “fun” looks in the summer, and you can get a little more creative with the materials (linen, seersucker, etc.). Fall weddings are typically a little more buttoned-up, but there’s a little wiggle room there, too.

I’ll go through some of the easiest ways for guys to dress for an autumn affair—with different wedding types in mind—to get you off the ground. We also included plenty of price points because, as everyone knows, weddings can get expensive fast.

Brooks Brothers Explorer Collection Non-Iron Twill Button Down Collar

Cole Haan Men's Grand Neoclassic Plain Toe Oxfords

We’ll start with what we consider a traditional wedding: a separate ceremony at a church, chapel, or the wedding venue without a black-tie dress code. This is about as classic as it gets, so you don’t have to go overboard—but we do recommend wearing a timeless suit. Our style team has tested plenty of affordable menswear brands offering solid options that approximate the look and fit of made-to-measure tailoring. One of them is the Black Tux, an upstart that offers suits for both rental and purchase, with virtual and in-person fittings to match you with the closest standard size. The prices are great, too: the Essential Suit is just under $300 all in. We also happened to score a 20 percent off code for the Black Tux, made exclusively for Men’s Health readers. Just use code MH20 at checkout (minimum of $295). The code’s good until October 31. Most of its higher-priced suits also include a rental option, but for the extra $100 or so, we’d recommend just buying one. The True Navy is a safe color you can wear year-round. The Grey Suit is a step up and is made from a heavier—but still breathable—merino wool. Perfect for the autumn temperatures.

A classic dress shirt is more than okay, but if you want to stand out in an otherwise pretty basic look, you can go with a classic twill dress shirt like this one from Brooks Brothers. You can get a little bit more creative with the tie, but nothing too crazy; the left-to-right diagonal stripes of a classic rep tie keep it distinguished. A Classic Textured Solid Tie is always a safe bet, too. Baby blue and pink go well with a gray suit, and navy, black, and red look better with gray. The shoes are easy, too: black plain-toe oxfords for grays, and these simple brown Astorflex Loafers with a crisp navy blue.

Brooks Brothers Classic Fit Double-Breasted Wool Pinstripe 1818 Suit

Charles Tyrwhitt Cotton Pocket Square - White

Mack Weldon Silver Extended Crew Dress Sock

The Black Tux Picture Frame Brushed Gold Tie Bar

Black-tie affairs probably require even less creativity, but there are definitely ways to push the envelope to stand out. The safe choice, of course, is the classic tux. If you plan to need one on multiple occasions, we also love that the Black Tux once again gets top marks; its Essential option is also under $300. There are some pricier options you can also rent, but the Essential Tux is low-key enough to rock at any formal occasion. SuitShop is another upstart offering ready-to-wear tuxedos at accessible prices, including several options under $300. Accessories-wise, you can opt for a super fancy pair of onyx cufflinks from one of our favorite watch brands, Shinola, but something a little more budget-friendly is more than okay.

Nowadays, you don’t have to go all-black, at least depending on the event. But if you do deviate, you'd better make it count. Like upgrading to a double-breasted suit, for example. The Classic Fit Double-Breasted Wool Pinstripe 1818 Suit elevates your look without making you look like a Prohibition-era mobster (surprisingly, a very fine line).

The other big component of all of this: your shoes. You probably don’t want to go with a loafer; an oxford or derby shoe is the better option. Our favorite: Cole Haan’s Hawthorne Oxfords, a classic dress shoe that’s made with the brand’s famously comfortable insoles so your dogs will stay happy for hours. It’s also versatile enough to wear at dressy events or in a more casual office vibe. In other words, you’ll be getting a lot of use out of it.

If you want to go all out, you can go full custom. Go big or go home, as they say. If you’re in the NYC area, Alan David Custom is a great choice. The bespoke tailor will give you a sample suit to try on before making final decisions, and the experience is a throwback to classier times. They’ll even ship it to you when it’s all said and done. If you want to go fully custom, you’ll also need the shoes to match.

Bonobos Empire Stretch Italian Wool Tuxedo

Todd Snyder Italian Lightweight Sutton Jacket

Quince Supima Cotton Herringbone Dress Shirt

Todd Snyder Relaxed Fit Japanese Selvedge Chino

Reigning Champ Stretch Chino Marina Standard Pant

Allen Edmonds Rhett Cap-toe Oxford Dress Shoe

Cocktail weddings give you a little more freedom than a traditional one. Here, you can rock a classic suit or a nice blazer and slacks, and you wouldn’t be wrong either way. The classic Ludlow tux from J.Crew gives off serious old-school cocktail jacket vibes, and it’s reserved for swankier occasions. Todd Snyder’s Italian Lightweight Sutton Jacket is another high-end option that’s both breathable and easy to wear throughout the night. If you wear blazers regularly, you’ll also get plenty of use out of this, even into the hotter months. Todd Snyder also makes our favorite pair of relaxed-fit chinos that check a lot of boxes for us. The Relaxed Fit Japanese Selvedge Chino is a steep departure from the ones we wear to the office, which is why it’s such a legit option for dressier occasions.

If the baggier fit (and higher price tag) is scaring you off a bit, Reigning Champ makes an ultra-breathable cotton-twill chino that wears more like a standard dress pant. They’re comfortable, breathable, and have a little added stretch; you’ll get a lot of use out of them outside the wedding. The other big component of all of this: your shoes. You probably don’t want to go with a loafer; an Oxford or derby shoe is the better option. Our style team loves Allen Edmonds’. It’s made with calfskin leather, with a surprisingly light-yet-cushioned outsole that’s comfortable enough to use all night.

Billy Reid Exploded Glen Plaid Archie Jacket

Brooks Brothers Straight-Fit Cotton Advantage Chino Pants

Brooks Brothers Friday Shirt, Oxford Patterns

Madewell Johnny-Collar Sweater Polo in Slub Knit Cotton

Cole Haan Zerogrand Remastered Wing Tip Oxford

Barns have since had a huge come-up and are now a hugely popular wedding venue. Regardless of your stance on barn weddings, you have to dress a little differently. Vineyard weddings (and really any outdoor event) live in that same category. If you’re looking at a late-fall event, you’ll want something a little warmer. The Grey Plaid Wool Suit is a step up in that department without being too overbearing; the subtle designs also scream fall. You can also go with the blazer-and-dress-pants route. Abercrombie’s A&F Collins Blazer is a fantastic budget option, and the Olive Stripe colorway similarly gives off fall vibes. It’s easy to pair with dressier chinos, like the Straight-Fit Cotton Advantage Chino Pants from Brooks Brothers. They’re essentially dress pants with a certain chinoesque comfort.

If you do go this route, you can have a little fun with the undershirt; Brooks Brothers’ Friday Shirt can add some flair to your getup. Madewell’s Johnny-Collar Sweater Polo is also a nice departure from your traditional button-down (and a lot more comfortable, too). If the wedding isn’t all that fancy, you can get away with rocking some of the most comfortable dress shoes/sneakers out there: Cole Haan’s Zerogrand Remastered Wing Tip Oxfords.

Buck Mason Capitola Linen Carry-On Jacket

Bonobos Stretch Weekday Warrior Dress Pants

Reigning Champ Heavyweight Jersey OG T-Shirt

The destination wedding can definitely be a challenge, depending on how close you are to the person (or people) getting married. They’re always a great time, though, and you can get similarly creative. We suggest a travel blazer; you’re already shelling out a lot of money for flights and accommodations, so you can save a few bucks by not checking a full suit. Our style director, Christian Gollayan, recently did a full review of the Bonobos Jetsetter Knit Blazer. He described it as a “lifesaver” when traveling. You can definitely rock it at a fall destination wedding, especially considering the hardworking knit construction. For a lighter, beachy vibe, Buck Mason’s Capitola Linen Carry-On Jacket is my own go-to. It holds its shape well for linen, and some of the darker colors work well for any season.

Pants are easy to pack, so we’d suggest going with something that helps you stand out. You don’t want to go with something too casual, and the Heavyweight Jersey OG T-Shirt from Reigning Champ is anything but. It’s well-made, fits like a glove, and is a great way to show off some jewelry if you like to wear a chain or two.

#4845. RJ Mitte's Death Highlights Mental Health Challenges for People With Cerebral Palsy

Follow Healthline on our socials for all things health.

“Breaking Bad” actor and disability advocate RJ Mitte has died at age 34.

Mitte reportedly died by suicide, his representative told People on October 12. However, local authorities have said the official cause and manner of his death remain under investigation.

Mitte, who was best-known for playing Walter White Jr. on the Emmy Award-winning television series “Breaking Bad,” lived with cerebral palsy and advocated for disability inclusion.

There is currently no evidence to suggest that cerebral palsy caused the actor’s death. Still, Mitte’s untimely passing highlights the mental health challenges that people with cerebral palsy may face.

Research has demonstrated elevated risks of anxiety and depression among those with the condition, alongside barriers to diagnosis, social participation, and employment.

“Living with cerebral palsy can affect mental health through several interacting pathways,” said Shannel Elhelou, neuropsychologist and founder of Brain Centric Neuropsychology in Westlake Village, CA.

“Chronic pain, fatigue, disrupted sleep, and the effort required to navigate daily activities can take an emotional toll. Experiences of bullying, discrimination, social exclusion, and difficulty accessing care can add to that burden. Also, the early brain injury underlying cerebral palsy may contribute to difficulties with emotional regulation, although each person’s experience is different,” Elhelou told Healthline.

If you or someone you know is in crisis and considering suicide or self-harm, please seek support:

If you’re calling on behalf of someone else, stay with them until help arrives. You may remove weapons or substances that can cause harm if you can do so safely.

If you’re not in the same household, stay on the phone with them until help arrives.

Mitte played a key role in challenging stereotypes by portraying a teenager with cerebral palsy on “Breaking Bad.”

Outside of acting, Mitte advocated for people with disabilities through organizations including United Cerebral Palsy (UCP) and Shriners Children’s.

He also led the Mitte Foundation, a non-profit corporation founded in 1994 by his grandparents, Roy F. and Joann Cole Mitte, that improves the quality of life for people in Central Texas.

Mitte’s advocacy emphasized representation, inclusion, and opportunities for people with disabilities.

The legacy he leaves behind underscores the need to recognize mental health as an essential part of care for individuals with cerebral palsy and other disabilities.

Cerebral palsy (CP) is a group of conditions affecting movement, posture, and coordination.

Most people with cerebral palsy have typical intelligence, although some also have intellectual disabilities or other comorbid physical and mental health conditions.

A 2018 study published in JAMA Neurology found that adults with cerebral palsy had a 28% higher risk of developing depression and a 40% higher risk of anxiety than adults without the condition.

A 2024 study in JAMA Network Open found higher recorded rates of anxiety and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) among children and young adults with cerebral palsy.

The researchers also identified comparatively low rates of depression and suicidal ideation, highlighting concerns that these conditions may be underdiagnosed.

“Research shows that adults with cerebral palsy have an increased risk of depression and anxiety,” Elhelou said.

“However, these conditions should never be viewed as an inevitable part of having a disability. One concern is ‘diagnostic overshadowing,’ when symptoms of depression, anxiety, or other mental health conditions are attributed to cerebral palsy itself, leading those conditions to go unrecognized and untreated. Someone’s fatigue, withdrawal, or changes in behavior deserve careful assessment rather than the assumption that ‘this is just their cerebral palsy,'” she continued.

“While these findings help us understand mental health risks among people with cerebral palsy, they cannot tell us what any one person was experiencing. Many interacting factors may contribute to someone dying by suicide, and it would be inappropriate to attribute an individual’s death to their disability.”

A 2019 study published in Developmental Medicine & Child Neurology found that children with cerebral palsy had higher odds of anxiety disorders and behavioral challenges than children without the condition.

Difficulties with friendships and bullying were associated with some of these differences.

Factors that may affect well-being include:

The researchers also found that supportive friendships may help reduce some of these disparities, reinforcing the importance of inclusive schools and communities.

A 2021 study published in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine found that U.S. adults with disabilities faced increased risks of suicidal thoughts, planning, and attempts compared with adults without disabilities.

The 988 Lifeline received more than 8 million contacts through calls, texts, chats, and American Sign Language videophone in 2025, according to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration.

Federal funding for the Lifeline’s dedicated LGBTQ+ youth service ended in July 2025, removing the option to press 3 for specialized support.

After pressure from Congress, the service was recently restored at the end of September, according to the Kaiser Family Foundation (KFF).

Employment and financial independence can influence well-being for anyone, particularly those with cerebral palsy.

However, a 2024 study found that just 30.4% of young adults with cerebral palsy who participated in vocational rehabilitation programs were employed when they exited those programs.

Workplace accommodations, accessible hiring, vocational rehabilitation, and inclusive social opportunities can help address these barriers.

“Depression and anxiety are treatable, and they should never be dismissed as an inevitable part of living with a disability,” Elhelou said.

“If you notice persistent sadness, anxiety, hopelessness, or withdrawal, reach out to someone you trust and a mental health professional. You deserve a clinician who takes your concerns seriously and adapts treatment to your communication, mobility, or other access needs. Care should also address pain, fatigue, and sleep difficulties, which can affect emotional well-being.”

Organizations such as United Cerebral Palsy offer information and support for people with cerebral palsy and their families.

Healthcare professionals can also improve outcomes by screening for mental health concerns, using appropriate assessment tools, and connecting patients with accessible treatment.

Improved access to care, inclusive communities, and meaningful opportunities can help people with cerebral palsy and other disabilities thrive.

“Asking for help does not diminish your resilience or your contributions. If you are experiencing thoughts of suicide or feel overwhelmed, you do not have to wait until things feel unbearable to reach out,” Elhelou said.

“Supportive relationships, peer groups, and disability communities can offer connection and understanding. Staying engaged in activities that bring enjoyment and meaning can also help.”

#4844. Nickey Kehoe’s New Collection With The Lacquer Company Takes Its Cues From Beloved Antiques

In 2024, AD heralded the return of lacquer. In our April 2026 issue, cover star Athena Calderone was pictured leaning over an enormous burgundy-lacquered kitchen island, and in May, cover star Mark Grattan showed off his parrot green lacquer walls. Today’s collaboration between AD100 design firm Nickey Kehoe and The Lacquer Company brings the glossy finish down to a slightly more manageable scale, applying it to coffee tables, desks, trays, and tissue boxes. Nickey Kehoe founders Todd Nickey and Amy Kehoe designed the 30-piece collection with The Lacquer Company founder James Lowther, drawing on antique furniture and objects the three have collected over the years.

The Bonne Nuit nightstand in Cassis staged among various Nickey Kehoe textiles and an upholstered headboard.

The Florin Tray in Carreaux & Marine Blue is styled with all small pieces from the Nickey Kehoe collection.

Many of the pieces, as is often true of Nickey Kehoe’s in-house catalog, draw on the founders’ personal vintage collections. The Pastis side table is based on a bamboo folding table that belongs to Nickey. The Hugo desk is a Louis XVI–style writing desk, with tapered, fluted legs, brass details, and three soft-close drawers in a bright red lacquer. The colorways sound like a very civilized, French late lunch: cassis and lettuce green, carreaux and marine blue, khaki and chocolate brown. The Jules catchall tray comes with a matching tissue box cover for the powder room.

Lacquer trays, tissue boxes, side tables, and the collection’s coffee table are staged together here to show the full line.

The Pastis side table references a vintage style with the lacquer and bamboo combination reminiscent of Regency Chinoiserie.

Lowther bought his first piece of lacquer, a burnt-orange betel box, while traveling in Burma in 1999, and it’s still one of his favorite things. He later found the craftspeople he was looking for in Saigon, and every piece from The Lacquer Company is still made there in Sơn Mài lacquer, a Vietnamese art form that goes back centuries. The process is lengthy: Wood is first sealed with a resin called Sinh. It’s then coated repeatedly with natural lacquer mixed with ground mountain rock, alluvial soil, and cashew nut shell oil. Each coat is wet-sanded until it’s smooth before the next coat is applied. “There is no prescribed drying time, no set number of layers,” according to the company. That makes the eight- to 12-week lead time on larger pieces easier to forgive.

Nickey Kehoe’s goal is for its furniture to feel “as if it was acquired, not purchased.” With these pieces so rooted in vintage styles and techniques, they make good on their promise.

The collection is available to shop on NickeyKehoe.com.

Follow Healthline on our socials for all things health.

Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer following a successful surgery, the Vatican said.

The Pope, 71, underwent surgery at Agostino Gemelli University Policlinic in Rome on October 13 to remove a nodule from his right lung. This was determined to be pulmonary adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer.

The surgeons removed the lower lobe of the Pope’s lung to “ensure a radical procedure; the lower lobe of the right lung was removed using a video-assisted technique,” said Dr. Luigi Carbone, the Director of Vatican Healthcare Services, and Professor Stephano Margaritora, the lead surgeon, in a press release.

“An intraoperative histological examination confirmed the diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, as suspected from the preoperative examinations,” they said.

Pope Leo was in the operating room for 3 hours, while the operation itself lasted around 90 minutes.

The doctors noted that it was a successful operation with no complications.

According to Matteo Bruni, the Director of the Holy See Press Office, the Pope asked for dinner after the surgery and spent the evening with his secretaries and other Vatican staff.

In a press release on Wednesday, the Vatican said that the Pope’s postoperative recovery is progressing well.

According to Vatican News, Pope Leo had a calm first night following his surgery.

In the coming days, exams will be conducted on the removed tissue. There has currently been no change in the initially announced week of hospitalization.

On October 14, the Pope underwent blood tests and chest X-rays that were scheduled following his surgery. The results of these tests confirm that his postoperative recovery is progressing as expected, and the values are within a normal range for the type of operation performed.

Pope Leo has also undergone some respiratory physiotherapy and has begun walking around his room, the Vatican said.

It has not yet been announced whether he will require any further treatment.

Adenocarcinoma is the most common subtype of lung cancer globally. It accounts for around 40% of all lung cancer diagnoses.

Adenocarcinoma is a type of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), which accounts for about 80–85% of all lung cancers.

Lung adenocarcinoma begins in the epithelial cells that produce mucus. It is the most common type of NSCLC.

Adenocarcinoma can be classified further by the genetic changes driving the tumor. For example, EGFR-positive lung cancer is found more often in people who have never smoked and can often be treated with targeted therapies, which is why biomarker testing of tumor tissue helps guide treatment decisions.

Treatment for NSCLC is generally determined by the stage. However, it typically involves one or a combination of:

Surgery is generally the first step in treatment for this type of lung cancer. The right lung has three lobes, or sections, and the left has two.

A doctor will often remove the entire lobe that has the tumor in order to remove the tumor and improve the outlook.

The body eventually adapts in order to compensate for the loss of function.

According to the American Cancer Society (ACS), for NSCLC that hasn’t spread outside of the lung, the 5-year relative survival rate is 67%.

#4841. Fitbit Edge vs. Fitbit Air: Which New Fitbit Should You Buy?

Do you want a less distracting tracker or one with a screen and built-in GPS?

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

GOOGLE DIDN’T RELEASE a major new Fitbit fitness tracker for two and a half years after the Charge 6 came out in October 2023. Then it released two new models in five months. The first, the $99 Fitbit Air, came out in May and works a lot like a Whoop. You wear it day and night, and it sends your heart rate, sleep, and workout data to the Google Health app on your phone.Second is the $179 Fitbit Edge, which followed in October as the Charge 6’s successor. It offers the same features as the Air and adds a 1.34-inch screen, built-in GPS, and an ECG app that checks your heart rhythm for signs of atrial fibrillation, an irregular heartbeat that raises your stroke risk. Both trackers pair with iPhones and Android phones, so neither is exclusive to Google’s platform.For most people, deciding between them comes down to one question: do you want to see your pace and heart rate on your wrist during a workout, or are you fine checking everything on your phone afterward?

With no screen and no buttons, the Fitbit Air is as simple as they come to use. Google rates its battery at up to seven days, so you won’t have to charge every night. It’s also the cheaper way to get Google’s Health Coach. The $99 price includes three free months of Google’s Health Premium, which costs $9.99 a month after that.The Fitbit Edge shows your pace and heart rate on its screen during a workout, and its built-in GPS records your route without your phone. If you run or ride outdoors, you can leave your phone at home and still come back with a map and split times. The Edge also has two sensors the Air doesn’t: electrical sensors for the ECG app, and an altimeter that measures elevation gain on a hike and counts the floors you climb. It costs $80 more than the Air, and turning on its always-on display cuts the battery from about seven days to about two.

The Air’s tracker module is a 1.37 x 0.66-inch pod, and it’s about 25 percent smaller than the discontinued Fitbit Luxe. The pod pops out of its band and snaps into another one in a few seconds, so you can wear the fabric Performance Loop to sleep and switch to the silicone Active Band for a sweaty workout. If you want something dressier, the polyurethane Elevated Modern Band and a new Metal Mesh band are also available.The Edge measures 1.54 x 1.01 inches and is almost half an inch thick, with a pill-shaped body that’s noticeably larger than the Air. A side button opens the app list and takes you back to the clock face. It comes in Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon, with six band styles that run from the sweat-resistant Active Sport Band to a Metal Links bracelet. Both trackers are rated IP68 and 5ATM, which means they have dust and water protection.

The Fitbit Air and Fitbit Edge record the same health data. Both measure your heart rate around the clock, plus blood oxygen, overnight skin temperature changes, and heart rate variability (HRV), the variation in time between heartbeats. HRV usually drops when you’re stressed, sick, or haven’t recovered from hard training.The Google Health app uses those readings to set a Readiness score each morning. It also tracks Cardio Load, which estimates how much cardiovascular strain your workouts create, while your personalized weekly target helps you balance activity and recovery. It can help you spot changes in your training load, but it can’t tell you exactly what your body can handle. Both trackers can alert you to an irregular rhythm that could be atrial fibrillation. They can also notify you when your heart rate stays unusually high or low while you’re inactive. Both also have Smart Wake, which vibrates to wake you during light sleep inside a time window you set.The Edge adds a few health tools the Air doesn’t have. Its ECG app records your heart’s electrical activity whenever you start a reading. If your heart feels like it’s racing or skipping, you can take a reading in the moment and save it to show your doctor. The Edge has a dedicated skin-temperature sensor, while older Fitbits such as the Charge 6 use a device-temperature sensor to track overnight skin-temperature variation.With Google Health Premium, both trackers get Google’s advanced Health Guardian features, which track trends in your blood pressure and insulin resistance. Google says they aren’t meant to screen or diagnose any condition.Both trackers start logging common workouts on their own. In my testing, the Air logged walks and lifting sessions without my starting them. Google says an update expands automatic detection on both the Air and Edge from 10 workout types to more than 100, including strength training, swimming, and racket sports. A workout only gets logged automatically if it lasts at least 15 minutes and keeps your heart rate up, so you may have to log short or stop-and-start sessions yourself.

The Fitbit Edge has built-in GPS, so it can map your route and measure your pace and distance without your phone. Google says the Edge’s GPS is up to 40 percent more accurate than its earlier trackers, thanks to a new GPS chip and case design. The Edge also has an altimeter, which reads air pressure to measure how much elevation you gain on a hilly run or how many floors you climb on a stair workout.The Edge’s screen also shows your stats during a workout, giving you instant feedback. You can set a pace target before a run and check on the screen whether you’re ahead of pace or lagging behind. During HIIT intervals, you can see which heart rate zone you’re in. On the track, it shows your split for each lap.The Fitbit Air has no GPS and no screen. To map a run, you have to carry your phone, and you can’t check your pace or heart rate until you look at the Google Health app afterward. If you mostly lift or walk and don’t want instant feedback, the Air is a great option. But if you care about your splits, the Edge is the better tracker.

The Fitbit Edge comes with nine apps, including Google Maps, Weather, and Timer. You can’t download more, and unlike the Pixel Watch 5, it doesn’t let you talk to Gemini from your wrist. Google Maps shows turn-by-turn directions on the Edge only after you start navigation on your phone, so you can’t look up a destination on the tracker itself.Calls and texts from your phone show up on the Edge’s screen. On Android, you can answer a text with a preset reply like “on my way.” Those quick replies don’t work with an iPhone, so iPhone owners can read texts on the Edge but have to answer them on the phone. Swiping down on the Edge opens a control panel where you can turn on Do Not Disturb, use the screen as a flashlight, or make your phone ring when you can’t find it.The Fitbit Air has none of this. Its only feature you’ll notice day to day is the Smart Wake alarm, which vibrates to wake you up. Everything else, including the Health Coach, lives in the Google Health app, which also syncs with Apple Health if you want your data in one place on an iPhone.Neither tracker has NFC, so you can’t use either one to pay with Google Wallet.

You don’t need a subscription to use either tracker. Without one, the Google Health app still shows your steps, heart rate, HRV, blood oxygen, sleep score and stages, Readiness, Cardio Load, and workouts. It also alerts you to an irregular heart rhythm. Google Health Premium costs $9.99 a month, and the Air and Edge each come with three months free.Premium adds the Gemini-powered Health Coach, which you can message anytime with questions about your data, plus weekly workout plans that adjust to your schedule. When I told it my shoulder was sore, it reworked that week’s plan around it. It also adds more detailed sleep summaries, meal logging from a photo, and plain-language summaries of your lab results.

The Charge 6 came out in 2023 and retails for $159.95. It has an ECG app and built-in GPS, and it can track more than 40 types of exercise. The Fitbit Edge improves on almost all of that. Its screen is 46 percent bigger, it’s rated IP68 for dust resistance, and it charges in about 90 minutes instead of two hours. And when the Edge’s battery wears out, you can replace it yourself instead of buying a new tracker.The Edge does drop two features the Charge 6 offers. The first is NFC, the chip that lets you pay with Google Wallet. The second is the EDA Scan app, which measures small changes in the sweat on your skin to estimate your stress level. If you’re buying a new tracker, the Charge 6 makes sense only if you pay with your wrist or find it well below the Edge’s $179 price (it’s down to $129.95 on Google’s site at the time of publication).The Fitbit Inspire 3 is the cheapest Fitbit with a screen, at about $100. It’s smaller than the Charge 6, lasts longer between charges, and starts tracking walks and runs automatically. It has no GPS or ECG, but it remains a solid choice if you want to see the time and your step count on your wrist without paying for the Edge.

Buy the Fitbit Air if you lift, walk, or take classes and mostly want to know how well you slept and how hard to train each day. At $99, it gets you the same heart rate, HRV, and sleep data as the Edge, and the same Health Coach if you pay for Premium. Because it has no screen, nothing on your wrist lights up or buzzes during dinner or in the middle of the night.For $80 more than the Air, the Edge gets you built-in GPS that maps your route and measures your pace without your phone. The screen shows your splits and heart rate zones while you’re moving, and the altimeter counts the elevation you climb. The ECG app also lets you check your heart rhythm the moment something feels off.If you already have a Charge 6, you don’t have to upgrade to get Google’s newest software. The Health Coach and Premium features come through the Google Health app, so they work on the tracker you already own. Upgrade to the Edge if the Charge 6’s battery no longer gets you through the week. But it’s worth keeping if you pay with your wrist. Neither new Fitbit has NFC, so the Charge 6 is the only one of the three that works with Google Wallet.

#4840. How One Designer Brought a Discerning Eye to Her Deeply Personal Manhattan Apartment

Ask an interior designer about their most difficult client, and there’s a good chance they’ll name themselves. Dani Dennis spent more than a decade at Mark Cunningham Inc. before founding her own New York–based practice, Danielette Dennis Interiors, translating other people’s tastes into rooms. “I’m such a decisive person,” she says of her approach to projects ranging from a traditional Brooklyn Heights townhouse to a sleek Park Avenue pied-à-terre. But when it came to decorating her own Gramercy Park apartment that she shares with her husband and two daughters, Dennis had no client brief to answer to—and no one to make the final call but herself.

When the family moved in three years ago, the apartment had plenty going for it: tall windows, handsome moldings, and an airy living and dining area. Dennis left the architecture alone, putting furniture, textiles, and her growing art collection to work instead. Benjamin Moore’s Steam keeps the walls a warm white, though the rooms are anything but hands-off. “I almost wanted it to feel like a gallery,” she says. “But, obviously, it’s lived in, and I have kids, so nothing is too precious.”

A portrait by Patrick Eugène, sourced via Mariane Ibrahim, anchors one end of the living room. Nearby are an Alfred Grenander chair upholstered in Toyine Sellers fabric, a black mushroom side table by Emma Donnersberg, and Christian Woo’s Noga Cube side table.

A portrait of a young girl by Jerrell Gibbs hangs near a Pierre Augustin Rose Cadillac ottoman upholstered in Rosemary Hallgarten’s alpaca bouclé. Vintage Saint-Louis crystal, sourced at the Paris flea market, sits atop the credenza.

The living room’s opposing sofas encourage conversation. The sofa (right), upholstered in Pierre Frey wool and mohair, is by Marked NYC. The ceiling fixture is a reedition of Pierre Chareau’s Quart de Rond lamp, and the rug is by Scott Group Studio.

Joseph-André Motte chairs surround the dining table, while a 1960s Italian burlwood credenza from Naga Antiques sits beneath an abstract painting by Carmen Neely. The dining rug is by Crosby Street Studios.

A first-generation American of Liberian heritage, Dennis has built a collection of art that includes contemporary Black artists from across the diaspora. A painting of girls playing in a circle takes her back to her school days in Côte d’Ivoire. Others show Black women in moments of rest and repose. “I want my kids and my family to be surrounded by reflections of us,” she says. Her clients’ collections tell their own stories; this one tells hers. Black joy runs through the collection, but Dennis doesn’t shop by theme; she listens to her gut. “I buy what I love,” she says. “I don’t buy for decoration.”

Dennis is equally at ease with an English-country chintz and a graphic geometric. In her own home, she borrows a little from everywhere, favoring clean lines and unexpected combinations. A custom sofa in Sanderson velvet faces a curved Marked NYC design in Pierre Frey wool and mohair. Camel-colored lounge chairs play against the sharp geometry of a Roger Sprunger coffee table; a 1906 Josef Hoffmann side table and an early-20th-century Alfred Grenander chair join the mix. “When the harmony comes from shape and proportion and feeling, I think that’s what makes spaces dynamic,” she says.

An expressive Ferrari Sheppard painting, acquired through Massimo De Carlo in Milan, hangs above a custom sofa upholstered in Sanderson’s indigo Quartz velvet. Camel-colored chairs wear Holland & Sherry fabric. A glass-and-metal coffee table by Roger Sprunger joins a modernist stool by Charles Vandenhove and JM Szymanski’s slender Table No. 3.

Dennis took a moodier approach in the library, where the family gathers. The walls and ceiling are painted the same dark hue, creating a cozy retreat for her two daughters, who prefer sprawling on the soft rug to sitting on the sofa. Artwork includes a floral painting by Alexandria Tarver and Hazel Mphande’s Stone or Lavender (2021). The striped pillows are in Fortuny fabric.

The dining table seats 10. Dinner guests, however, are still forthcoming. “I haven't had people over yet, because in my head it’s not done,” Dennis says. Joseph-André Motte chairs surround the table, while a 1960s Italian burlwood credenza and a Crosby Street Studios rug anchor the dining area. The living room sofas were positioned for entertaining too, although the family’s day-to-day use of the space is less formal. For Dennis’s daughters, 10 and seven, the mohair-and-wool sofa comes with ground rules: “You guys can sit on it, you can perch, but if we want to play, let’s do it elsewhere.”

The library, on the other hand, is fair game. The girls can sprawl out with a book or watch TV, though they rarely bother with the sofa. “They’re always lying on the rug,” Dennis says. She painted the walls a deep olive-green, carrying it across the ceiling for an enveloping effect. The art also takes a moodier turn, with a floral painting by Alexandria Tarver and a black-and-white self-portrait by Hazel Mphande. The primary bedroom, meanwhile, provides a brighter, quieter escape. “I always wanted to be in a cloud,” the designer says of the neutral palette. The upholstered bed, 1970s steel bench in alpaca wool, and leather-bound nightstands supply the texture.

Since the photo shoot, Dennis has switched out accessories and rearranged objects. When she recently swapped a lamp in the living room, even her husband took notice. “Another one?” he asked. At work, Dennis knows when to call a room finished. At home, she’s beginning to wonder why she should.

“I always wanted to be in a cloud,” Dennis says of the primary bedroom, where texture takes precedence over color. A vintage 1970s steel bench with alpaca upholstery sits at the foot of the bed, while leather-clad nightstands add another tactile element. The ceramic lamp is by Christiane Perrochon, and the understated artwork above the bed is by Carmen Neely.
